disposition_reason: Table 2 prints single concentrations of ten elements in five powdered flavor drinks bought in a Nigerian market.

study.design: Market survey of five powdered flavor drink products
study.method: Wet digestion of 1 g powder with HNO3/HCl/HClO4 (1:1:1), made up to 50 mL; flame AAS (AA320N)
study.qa: Distilled-water blank showed no detectable metal; no CRM, recovery or replicates reported

regulatory_or_exposure.what: US EPA (2011) drinking-water maximum contaminant levels used as comparator (Pb 0.015, Cd 0.005, As 0.01, Hg 0.002 mg/L)

unresolved: Results are mg/L of the digest solution (1 g in 50 mL), not of the reconstituted drink or the powder; no conversion to mg/kg is printed, so none was made.

Text ranges conflict with Table 2: text gives lead 0.040-0.199 and cadmium 0.075-0.260 mg/L, the abstract swaps them (cadmium 0.040-0.199, lead 0.075-0.260); Table 2 gives cadmium 0.075-0.260 and lead 0.048-0.199 mg/L. Table values were used.
Abstract gives nickel 0.091-0.1324 mg/L; Table 2 maximum is 1.324 mg/L. Conclusion gives arsenic 0.221-0.185 mg/L (typo for 1.185).
Abstract names the digestion acids as HNO3, H2SO4 and HClO4; Methods say HNO3, HCl and HClO4.
Mercury by flame AAS at 0.13-0.49 mg/L is not supported by any described cold-vapour method; no LOD or QA is given, so all values are of uncertain reliability.
Five flavoring agents (coconut, pineapple, orange, cola, mango) are listed but not mapped to product codes.
